arml-2005-superrelay-01.title: AM-GM
arml-2005-superrelay-01.body:
$\frac12bh=200$ so $bh=400$. By AM-GM, $b+h\ge2\sqrt{bh}=2\sqrt{400}=40$, with equality at $b=h=20$.

**Answer: 40**

arml-2005-superrelay-02.title: Evaluate the logarithms
arml-2005-superrelay-02.body:
*(In the relay $T=40$ was the answer to problem 1.)* $\log_2 32=5$, so $\log_4(40+x)=3$, hence $40+x=4^3=64$ and $x=24$.

**Answer: 24**

arml-2005-superrelay-03.title: Values of $f$
arml-2005-superrelay-03.body:
*(In the relay $T=24$ was the answer to problem 2.)* $K=48$. $f(n)=i^n+i^{-n}=2\cos\frac{n\pi}2$, which equals $2$ if $n\equiv0$, $0$ if $n$ is odd and $-2$ if $n\equiv2\pmod4$. $f(48)=2$, so we need $f(n)=-2$, i.e. $n\equiv2\pmod4$: $n=2,6,\dots,2002$, which is $\dfrac{2002-2}{4}+1=501$ values.

**Answer: 501**

arml-2005-superrelay-04.title: Substitute
arml-2005-superrelay-04.body:
*(In the relay $T=501$ was the answer to problem 3.)* $668-501=167>0$, so the expression is $\dfrac{501}{167}+\dfrac{501}{167}=3+3=6$.

**Answer: 6**

arml-2005-superrelay-05.title: Half-angle identity
arml-2005-superrelay-05.body:
*(In the relay $T=6$ was the answer to problem 4.)* With $3T=18^\circ$: $\csc18^\circ-\cot18^\circ=\dfrac{1-\cos18^\circ}{\sin18^\circ}=\tan9^\circ$ (half-angle formula). The smallest positive solution is $\theta=9^\circ$.

**Answer: 9**

arml-2005-superrelay-06.title: Pythagorean theorem
arml-2005-superrelay-06.body:
*(In the relay $T=9$ was the answer to problem 5.)* $PA=6$. The foot of the altitude is the center of the square, at distance $\frac{8\sqrt2}2=4\sqrt2$ from each vertex, so $h=\sqrt{36-32}=2$ and $\dfrac h{\sqrt2}=\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $\sqrt2$**

arml-2005-superrelay-07.title: Solve the intersections
arml-2005-superrelay-07.body:
*(In the relay $T=\sqrt2$ was the answer to problem 6.)* With $c=2005T$: $A$: $x+y=c$, $y-x=6T$ gives $A=\left(\frac{c-6T}2,\frac{c+6T}2\right)$; $B$: $y-x=T$ gives $B=\left(\frac{c-T}2,\frac{c+T}2\right)$. Then $AB=\sqrt{\left(\frac{5T}2\right)^2+\left(\frac{5T}2\right)^2}=\dfrac{5T}{\sqrt2}=5$.

**Answer: 5**

arml-2005-superrelay-08.title: Add rectangles

arml-2005-superrelay-09.title: Complete the square
arml-2005-superrelay-09.body:
*(In the relay $T=28$ was the answer to problem 10.)* $x^2=y^2+2\sqrt3y+28=(y+\sqrt3)^2+25\ge25$, with equality at $y=-\sqrt3$. The least positive $x$ is $5$.

**Answer: 5**

arml-2005-superrelay-10.title: Power reduction
arml-2005-superrelay-10.body:
*(In the relay $T=56$ was the answer to problem 11.)* $\sin^2\dfrac{k\pi}{14}=\dfrac{1-\cos\frac{k\pi}7}{2}$. The values $\cos\frac{k\pi}7$ repeat with period $14$ in $k$ and sum to $0$ over any $14$ consecutive terms (the angles are spread symmetrically around the circle). Since $56=4\cdot14$, the sum is $\dfrac{56}{2}=28$.

**Answer: 28**

arml-2005-superrelay-11.title: Arithmetic sequence
arml-2005-superrelay-11.body:
*(In the relay $T=3$ was the answer to problem 12.)* The $n$th term is $-5956+(n-1)T$, so the $2005$th is $-5956+2004\cdot3=-5956+6012=56$.

**Answer: 56**

arml-2005-superrelay-12.title: Group the pizzas
arml-2005-superrelay-12.body:
*(In the relay $T=1$ was the answer to problem 13.)* $K=11$. Each carload gives $11+1=12$ pizzas, so $36$ pizzas come from $36/12=3$ carloads.

**Answer: 3**

arml-2005-superrelay-13.title: Pythagorean identity
arml-2005-superrelay-13.body:
*(In the relay $T=\frac{3\sqrt2}8$ was the answer to problem 14.)* If $\theta=\sin^{-1}T$ then $\sin\theta=T$ and $\cos^2\theta+T^2=\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$.

**Answer: 1**

arml-2005-superrelay-14.title: Power of a point
arml-2005-superrelay-14.body:
*(In the relay $T=3$ was the answer to problem 15.)* $AB=6$. By symmetry about the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, $EA=BF=\frac{10-6}2=2$, so $BE=8$ and $BF=2$. The power of $B$ gives $BD\cdot BG=BE\cdot BF=16$. $BD=6\sqrt2$, so $BG=\dfrac{16}{6\sqrt2}=\dfrac{8}{3\sqrt2}$ and $\dfrac1{BG}=\dfrac{3\sqrt2}8$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{3\sqrt2}{8}$**

arml-2005-superrelay-15.title: Difference of squares
arml-2005-superrelay-15.body:
The first equation says $x^2-y^2=2005$ and the second $x-y=\dfrac{2005}3$. Then $x+y=\dfrac{x^2-y^2}{x-y}=\dfrac{2005}{2005/3}=3$.

**Answer: 3**
